Hi Monica,

Thanks for taking this. Carter Tech is moving fast on a pilot and we want to put together a Private Offer via AWS Marketplace. A couple of items procurement needs clarity on before we can finalize: 

- Net unit price for a 1 yr committed Dedicated capacity (estimate 200 GPU-hours/month).
- Any stacking rules if we also use a Redwood-hosted API for burst traffic.
- Channel commission expectations: our reseller is CloudScale Partners — they are asking for a 15%+ commission to support implementation and first-line support.
- Which discounts are applied on the AWS private offer vs. partner rebate (we need to know invoice flow).

Attached is our RFP (see Carter_Tech_RFP_Jun2026.pdf). Procurement would like a written outline we can include in the PO. Jenny, looping you in to ensure we follow the AWS PO/private-offer flow.

Best,

Bob — thanks, and welcome. Quick summary of where we land and what we need from you to lock a private offer: 

Proposal (initial):
- 12-month committed private offer for Dedicated capacity. Approx list price $0.95 / GPU-hour.
- Private offer discount off list: up to 22% depending on commit tier (we typically tier at $25k / $50k / $75k committed monthly spend).
- Channel commission: Redwood supports partner commissions paid as a rebate to the partner; typical bands 10% base, up to 18% for strategic deals with professional services included.

Request from Carter Tech:
- Confirm expected monthly committed spend (helps pick tier).
- Confirm whether CloudScale should be paid directly by Redwood (partner rebate) or via your PO flow.

Operational notes:
- For AWS private offers the discount is reflected in the private offer price. Partner commission is a separate rebate (we can handle through AWS Marketplace partner flow or a direct Redwood rebate — need to pick).
- If you plan to burst to hosted API, we recommend a soft-cap on burst spend so it doesn’t materially affect committed unit economics; we can include a burst-addendum in the term sheet.

I attached a pricing workbook (redwood_private_offer_pricing_v1.xlsx) and a short term-sheet draft. If you confirm monthly commit and preferred partner payout path, I’ll route for approvals.

Thanks,

Aditya / Lauren — forwarding Carter Tech thread. They asked for partner commission in the 15%+ range (CloudScale). Carter expects a private offer on AWS. High level:

- Estimated commit: Carter indicates pilot likely to convert to a $50k-$100k/mo commit if successful.
- CloudScale expects ~15–18% commission to cover onboarding and first-line ops.

Questions:
1) What commission cap can we authorize on marketplace private offers (if any) without eroding economics?
2) Is it acceptable to split discount: give Carter a 20% private-offer discount off list and separately give CloudScale a 16% partner rebate (so net to Redwood is X)?
3) Anything needed from Legal/RevOps to route rebates via AWS partner flow vs. direct Redwood invoice credit?

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Carter Tech private offer — channel margin ask

Monica — quick answers and approved guardrails: 

1) Commission cap: Approved up to 16% partner commission for deals meeting a minimum commit of $75k/month (12 month minimum). Below $75k/mo, cap is 10%. We need to protect unit economics so we want partner commission to be applied as a rebate on partner invoices (or via AWS partner payout) rather than reducing the private-offer price directly.

2) Discount split: Yes — go ahead with a private-offer discount (up to 22% off list for the right commit) and separately structure a partner rebate of up to 16% (rebate paid quarterly after invoice). Document that the partner rebate is contingent on partner providing onboarding and 24x5 support SLA for the first 90 days.

3) Ops/Legal asks:
- Lauren: can you confirm RevOps acceptance for the AWS partner payout flow vs Redwood direct rebate? We should prefer AWS partner payout where possible to avoid manual credits.
- Monica: require SOW signed and DocuSign PO routed through AWS private offer flow. Provide the DocuSign stub for signatures.

Also: price protect the deal by capping marketplace-facing list reduction to 22% and require a clause that rediscounts or retroactive credits need leadership signoff.

If that works I’ll approve the structure and you can share the term-sheet with Carter.

- Aditya
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
